h1: Hotel de Ladda Mukdahan — the 4-star riverside hotel where opening the balcony means a full view of the Mekong
intro: If you are coming to Mukdahan and want a riverside stay where pulling back the curtains reveals the Laos bank across the water, Hotel de Ladda is the name guests mention most. It is a 4-star hotel on Samran Chai Khong Road, opened in 2016, with 47 rooms. What guests love most: private Mekong-view balconies, floor-to-ceiling windows and marble bathrooms with a tub. There is an outdoor pool and gym looking onto the river, and the Indochine Market is a short walk away. From approx. THB 1,400/night.

body.html: Hotel de Ladda sits on Samran Chai Khong Road, right along the Mekong in central Mukdahan. The main draw is location and view — many rooms open onto balconies with a full sweep of the Mekong and the Laos bank opposite. The Indochine Market and the riverfront walking street, the town's main eating-and-strolling area, are just a few minutes on foot. It suits travellers who want a comfortable in-town base without driving out of the centre.

There are 47 rooms, from Superior and Deluxe Twin up to Premier Suite and Premier Corner Suite. Guests consistently praise the same things: spacious rooms, floor-to-ceiling windows that flood the room with light and frame the river, and marble bathrooms with both a tub and a strong rain shower. The corner suites get a dual-aspect view and are the rooms reviewers recommend most if the budget allows. In-room amenities are complete — fridge, minibar, flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi.
"Woke up, opened the curtains, and there was the sun rising over the Mekong. The view from the balcony felt like floating above the water — a morning I won't forget."

Beyond the rooms, the hotel has an outdoor pool and gym that look onto the river, a massage room, the De Paris restaurant with a bar/lounge, and room service. Breakfast is served set/buffet style from 7:00–10:00, and reviewers say there is a fair spread with some made-to-order items. There is free private parking too, which is handy for self-drivers or anyone heading on to the Friendship Bridge 2 border crossing.

Things to accept: several guests note that the walls are fairly thin and you can hear the room next door, which can disturb sleep when the hotel is full. Another point is that the balconies have great views but some lack a table and chairs, so you end up standing to take it in. The finishing and some décor are provincial-hotel in style, not as polished as a big Bangkok chain, and front-desk English can be limited at times, so international guests may need a little sign language.

On price, standard rooms start around THB 1,400–2,100/night depending on the season, with river-view suites and corner rooms going higher. Some reviewers feel low-season rates can look a touch high relative to what is actually open on the day, so it pays to compare a few platforms and check that the pool and gym are running before booking. The overall score is 9.4 from 52 reviews on Trip.com, and TripAdvisor rates it 4.2/5, #2 of 14 hotels in Mukdahan.

In short, Hotel de Ladda is a good fit for travellers who want an in-town riverside stay in Mukdahan with a strong view, spacious rooms, easy walks to the Indochine Market, and a pool to cool off in. For the quietest night, ask for a higher floor on the river side and avoid peak-full dates. The tip is to lock in a River View or Corner Suite at the time of booking, because the magic here is squarely the Mekong view from the balcony.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Hotel de Ladda Mukdahan

faq.q: Where is Hotel de Ladda in Mukdahan, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Hotel de Ladda is at 77 Samran Chai Khong Tai Road, Si Bun Ruang, Mueang Mukdahan, right on the Mekong. It's about a 5-minute walk to the Indochine Market and the riverfront walking street, and roughly 15 minutes by car to the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge 2 crossing into Savannakhet.

faq.q: How much does Hotel de Ladda cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start around THB 1,400/night for a Superior room. Deluxe Twin and river-view Premier Suites run roughly THB 1,700–2,200, and the Premier Corner Suite is around THB 2,800 and up. Prices vary by season — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Do all rooms at Hotel de Ladda have a Mekong view?
faq.a: No, not all. Many rooms have river-view balconies facing the Mekong and Laos, but some face the town. If the view matters, book a room marked River View or a Premier Corner Suite up front rather than asking at check-in.

faq.q: Does Hotel de Ladda have a pool and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both. There's an outdoor swimming pool and gym overlooking the Mekong, plus free private parking — convenient for self-drivers or anyone continuing to the Friendship Bridge 2 border.

faq.q: What should I know before staying at Hotel de Ladda?
faq.a: Reviewers note the walls are fairly thin so you can hear neighbouring rooms, and some balconies lack a table and chairs. Front-desk English can be limited at times. Ask for a higher floor on the river side for quiet, and confirm the pool and restaurant are open before booking.
